how: Explains recruiting participants through an OG logo and GREENWALL proposal addressed to anyone willing to join.
Explains a bare commitment to join the proposed green brick army without asking for anything in return.
Explains abandoning GreenWall lettering because the desired addition was too large for the available space.
Explains a member proposing a recognisable logo which other participants answer with collective commitment and practical work.
Allows proposing the mark and recruiting helpers to occupy the same turn rather than assuming two separately observable stages.
Explains uptake of the early proposal through replies offering defence and reporting active logo construction.
Explains the direct bare acceptance of a building call while preserving a neighbouring reply that makes acceptance conditional on sparing art.
Explains proposing and revising the logo's surrounds and adjoining words while specifying colours to prevent contributors undoing one another.
Explains reporting work already started and moving a border as observable contributions within continuing construction.
Explains publishing an off-platform template and mapping its image coordinates onto the canvas for public contributors.
Explains returning chat-made plans to the public thread and routing contributors back into chat as design discussion continues.
Limits template settlement to partially visible coordination because the published plan originated elsewhere and subsequent design alternatives remained under discussion.
Explains an acknowledged repair account whose apparent identity initially made its work look like griefing.
Distinguishes acknowledged use of another account for repair from verified automation or simultaneous multiplication of placement capacity.
Leaves formal decision procedures and the aggregate prevalence claim undecided because retrospective leadership credit and reported chat coordination do not expose how order was established.
Explains keeping the logo correct through watchers and repeated pixel repairs after a design is treated as provisionally done.
Allows defence and repair to overlap unfinished construction rather than beginning only after the room has a completed mark.
Leaves strain causing additional account use undecided because the repair account's user supplies no capacity-shortage explanation for choosing it.
Explains participants challenging attribution of damage and inspecting placers' posting histories while remaining unable to verify collective responsibility independently.
Explains adjusting placement after a neighbour's complaint and invoking agreements that protect the purple border and Mexican flag.
Includes border disputes generated by builders clearing neighbouring work rather than explaining every negotiation as a response to erosion of their own mark.
Limits negotiated restraint's reach to cooperating placers because participants report growth outside their control and incomplete repair despite agreements.
Explains conditional participation, explicit limits on expansion, apologies, and proposals to rebuild work harmed by the spreading wall.
Explains converting apology into repair by requesting a schematic, returning it to chat, and committing to rebuild the damaged neighbour.
Explains cooperative maintenance that permits erasing parts of one's own expanding pattern when retaining them would destroy neighbouring work.
Explains routing a harmed neighbour into chat for repair and receiving its explicit report that the work was fixed.
Explains a small alliance in which neighbouring builders reportedly entered the shared chat and reciprocally preserved each other's work.
Explains a participant's explicit account connecting neighbours' request in chat with reciprocal preservation while leaving the original deliberation unseen.
Leaves manpower shortage as an origin of outside help undecided because mutual preservation is described without that causal explanation.
Leaves shared threat as an origin of alliance undecided because the reported agreement specifies preservation without explaining its formation through a common attack.
Explains seeking host approval for additional representation and accepting a suggested location constrained by the host's territorial rules.
Distinguishes a broker's report of approval limits and a proposed southern location from demonstrated construction under granted host permission.
Explains brokerage by a participant who offers to vouch for a representative and relays the prospective host's approval constraints.
Explains incompatible claims to collective consent when one member accepts an unidentified ally and others explicitly reject that acceptance after identification.
Locates the consent dispute after a proposal and provisional acceptance rather than assuming a completed treaty whose binding authority was then rejected.
Limits the observed move to a member switching contributions after a lost slogan battle rather than a demonstrated whole-room relocation after logo destruction.
Explains individual retargeting from a lost wording contest to an alternative adjoining mark already being built.
Leaves insufficient hands causing a move undecided because a participant reports losing a slogan battle without attributing that loss to manpower.
Explains reported pattern copying by unaffiliated placers as a mechanism for expansion beyond the people negotiating restraint, without verifying who placed particular destructive pixels.
Connects participants' reports of pattern copying with continued encroachment despite restraint, treating the causal attribution as their explanation rather than verified placer identities.
Explains translating an existing fan identity into GREENWALL lettering, green bricks, and the language of watching the wall.
Leaves a pre-existing quarrel behind the attack unobserved because the targeting proposal names a logo without stating a prior dispute.
Leaves a prior tie naming the attack target unobserved because neither overwrite call supplies a historical or ideological reason in that turn.
Explains fake team news and rebranding through participants' recognition, evaluation, and eventual moderator disclosure of April Fools performance.
Explains removal of a canvas-find submission through the host's existing low-effort standard rather than a newly demonstrated canvas-specific rule.
Limits the evidenced response to ordinary-rule moderation because the removal does not establish canvas flooding as its cause.
Explains shared accomplishment through credit for leading, organising, contributing, and enjoying the collaborative project.
Explains participants contesting who earned collective credit through an exclusionary challenge and a counterclaim of greater activity.
Explains a success announcement that marks the completed logo while immediately recruiting further adjoining work.
Explains recording survival with a final image and timelapse while recounting nearby works' losses and takeovers.
Explains the previously unplaced mourning theme as remembrance of neighbouring art lost during the room's expansion.
Explains correcting the preserved account of apparent griefing through ownership identification and the user's explanation of repair, without establishing any shared-copy cleanup.
Leaves celebration causing preservation undecided because credit and a memorial timelapse coexist in one edited post rather than demonstrating the proposed causal sequence.
Distinguishes sharing an encountered third-party remake from evidence that the room decided to carry its own canvas effort into another medium.
Leaves a preserved record causing collective continuation undecided because the later post describes encountering a remake and the wish to continue supplies no decision.
Explains direct proposals to cover another logo and choose colours that outpace its defenders' repairs.
Allows an attack proposal to constitute recruitment itself rather than requiring evidence that previously assembled builders subsequently diverted their effort.
Explains a playful threat to a complaining neighbour as a limited verbal contest rather than evidence of an extended inter-room campaign.
Leaves attack causing sustained verbal rivalry undecided because an isolated threat and later internal expansion praise do not establish that causal mechanism.
Supports a reported chat decision to abandon an overwrite while leaving the missing intermediary reply and the deliberation's motives unresolved.
Supports invoking existing agreements against encroachment without assuming that attacking caused new negotiations or treaties.
Explains a member's wish to keep the activity going as a minimal continuation orientation without claiming collective commitment or realised new work.
Explains why removing one's own bricks to repair a neighbour requires distinguishing legitimate repair from apparent destruction of the wall.
Explains withholding cooperation when identifying a prospective ally reveals political or trust objections despite an earlier member's provisional acceptance.
